SPAN1401.description:
This unit offers an introduction to Spanish grammar and vocabulary to enable students to communicate both orally and in writing in simple situations. It develops cultural and linguistic awareness and focuses on contemporary spoken and written language used in Spain.

Students achieve language proficiency equivalent to Level A1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. The unit leads to SPAN1402 Spanish Studies 2.
SPAN1401.outcomes: Students are able to (1) demonstrate elementary skills in reading, writing, listening and speaking in the Spanish language; (2) demonstrate familiarity with sociolinguistic conventions in Spanish; (3) demonstrate an elementary knowledge of culture and society in Spanish-speaking countries; (4) use independent learning skills and interpersonal skills; and (5) demonstrate an increased awareness of language and language use in both Spanish and English.
SPAN1401.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) online/in-class test; (2) end of semester test; and (3) language compositions. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Student may be offered supplementary assessment in this unit if they meet the eligibility criteria.
SPAN1401.contactHours:
interactive lectures : 2 hours per week over 12 weeks
language classes: 2 hours per week over 12 weeks (involving a mix of formal instruction by the tutor, class discussion, group and pair work on linguistic and cultural themes, and oral presentations)
Summer—interactive lectures : 9 contact hours per week over 4 weeks
online language classes 3 hours per week
SPAN1401.courseNotes:
• Level 1 core unit in the Spanish Studies major sequence
  • Level 1 elective

SPAN1402.description:
This unit follows on from SPAN1401 Spanish Studies 1. It builds on the introduction to Spanish grammar and vocabulary, further developing students' ability to communicate orally and in writing in everyday situations. It focuses on contemporary spoken and written language used in Spain and uses authentic texts and audiovisual materials to deepen students' understanding of Spanish culture and society.

Students achieve language proficiency equivalent to Level A1/A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.
SPAN1402.outcomes: Students are able to (1) demonstrate elementary skills in reading, writing, listening and speaking in the Spanish language; (2) demonstrate familiarity with a broader range of sociolinguistic conventions in Spanish; (3) demonstrate an increased knowledge of culture and society in Spanish-speaking countries; (4) use independent learning skills and develop interpersonal skills; and (5) demonstrate an increased awareness of language and language use, in both Spanish and in English.
SPAN1402.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) online/in-class test; (2) language compositions; (3) end of semester test; and (4) portfolio. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Student may be offered supplementary assessment in this unit if they meet the eligibility criteria.
SPAN1402.contactHours:
online lectures : 2 hours per week over 12 weeks (1 hour culture and 1 hour language)
language classes: 2 hours per week over 12 weeks (involving a mix of formal instruction by the tutor, class discussion, group and pair work on linguistic and cultural themes, and oral presentations)
Summer—interactive lectures : 9 contact hours per week over 4 weeks
online language classes 3 hours per week
SPAN1402.courseNotes:
• Level 1 core unit in the Spanish Studies major sequence
  • Level 1 elective

SPAN1403.description:
This unit is intended for students with prior formal studies of Spanish (high school, WACE Spanish or equivalent). It develops the students' ability to communicate in Spanish by providing intensive practice in oral and written language, and enriches students' understanding of the cultures of modern Spain. This unit leads to SPAN1404 Spanish Studies 4.

Students achieve and consolidate their language proficiency at Level A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.
SPAN1403.outcomes: Students are able to (1) demonstrate competency in spoken and written Spanish that enables them to be confident users of the language in most situations they are likely to encounter in everyday life; (2) describe, make comparisons, suggestions and requests; (3) demonstrate an increased awareness of how language works in general (metalinguistic skills); (4) identify key historical, social and cultural aspects of Spanish society; and (5) demonstrate interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to work effectively in pairs and small groups.
SPAN1403.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) online/in-class test; (2) end of semester test; and (3) oral assessment. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Student may be offered supplementary assessment in this unit if they meet the eligibility criteria.
SPAN1403.contactHours:
interactive lectures: 1 hour per week
language classes: 2 hrs per week

It further develops the students' ability to communicate in Spanish by providing intensive practice in oral and written language, and enriches students' understanding of the culture of modern Spain.

Students achieve language proficiency equivalent to Level A2/B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

SPAN2812.description: This specialist unit, taught in Spanish, enables learners to consolidate their language competencies in writing, reading, listening and speaking through the critical analysis of textual, audio and visual sources from the media and the arts. Through the study of cultural sources, taken from the media and the arts, and related to topics ranging from geography, history and economy, through music, cinema and gastronomy, this unit allow students to engage with issues of contemporary significance in the Spanish-speaking world and to familiarize themselves with the breadth of Hispanic cultures.
SPAN2812.outcomes: Students are able to (1) develop oral and written skills in Spanish to Level A2/B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference of Languages; (2) broaden knowledge of Spanish-speaking cultures; (3) situate cultural sources in their regional, historical and cultural contexts; (4) develop intercultural competence; and (5) develop communication and interpersonal skills.
SPAN2812.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) in-class tests; (2) in-class participation; and (3) oral assessment. Further information is available in the unit outline.

SPAN3813.description: This specialist unit, taught in Spanish, enables learners to consolidate their language competencies in writing, reading, listening and speaking in Spanish through the critical analysis of literary works by authors from a range of Spanish-speaking countries. This survey of literature in Spanish introduces students to the breadth of literary expression in Spanish by studying a wide range of its forms and genres, typically including prose, poetic, musical and visual genres, allowing students to hone critical and analytical skills, and gain an understanding of the texts' contexts of production.
SPAN3813.outcomes:
Students are able to (1) develop oral and written skills in Spanish; (2) gain a panoramic knowledge of literature in Spanish; (3) situate literary texts in their historical, political, social and cultural contexts

; (4) learn specialised vocabulary associated with literary texts, forms, genres and styles; and (5) hone critical and analytical skills through the close reading of literary texts.
SPAN3813.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) in-class participation; (2) in-class test; and (3) oral presentation. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Student may be offered supplementary assessment in this unit if they meet the eligibility criteria.
SPAN3813.contactHours:
lectures: 1 hour per week (over 10 weeks)
tutorials: 1 x 2 hours per week (over 10 weeks)
SPAN3813.courseNotes:
• Level 3 core unit in the Spanish Studies major sequence
